conservation.condition_narrative:
- Paper is heavily cockled and wrinkled. 
- Shadows of hinges visible at top. 
- Bottom left corner bends upwards. 
- There are scattered slightly brown inclusions scattered throughout the paper 
- Thicker areas of paint have network cracking but are stable 
Frame is in very good condition.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Brooklyn Museum of Art in 2025.

materials.content: Watercolor and graphite on very thin, beige, very smooth laid paper, Japanese gampi (Source: Paper Survey researched by Judith C. Walsh and published in Lynes, 1999.)

cr_data.provenance: Until 1958 Downtown Gallery (The), New York, N.Y., then Purchased by Brooklyn Museum (The) (Source: Brooklyn Museum of Art, 2025)
remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive. Abiquiú Notebooks after 1977 indicates, "Sold by Halpert, April 1958." Missing label recorded in museum files: "Blue No IV/1916/watercolor, 11 x 16." Completed in Virginia before August move to Texas. Pictured in 1917 New York (291) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 4. See cat. nos. 91–93. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Two rounded forms, dark blue outside and fading to white at their centers, occupy the center of the composition. In the lower righthand corner, three blue brushstrokes move diagonally across the page.
